title: Prevalence of Hepatitis B Virus Infection Among Selected Pregnant Women Attending Antenatal Care a Within a Community Setting South-West Nigeria
content: The prevalence of HBV infection is increasing in our community particularly among pregnant women due to the high risk of vertical transmission. This study determine the prevalence of Hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg) among pregnant women attending selected antenatal care hospitals within Ede community, Osun State, Nigeria. A total of one-hundred & eighty (180) consenting pregnant women were recruited for the study. Blood samples were collected and analyzed using ELISA for HBsAg detection. Liver function was assessed in seropositive individuals using Alanine Aminotransferase (ALT) levels. The overall prevalence of HBsAg was 15.6% (28/180). Subjects aged 26–33 years had the highest rate of positivity at 50% of all positive cases. Statistical analysis showed a significant association between HBV infection and age group (χ² = 14.694, p = 0.618), blood transfusion (χ² = 0.972, p = 0.615), herbal medicine use (χ² = 1.843, p = 0.398), alcohol consumption (χ² = 0.291, p = 0.589), HBV awareness (χ² = 2.710, p = 0.100), vaccination status (χ² = 3.070, p = 0.576), and pregnancy per trimester (χ² = 1.126, p = 0.569). However, there was a statistical significant positive correlation between HBV infection and elevated ALT levels (r = 0.489, p = 0.007), suggesting possible liver inflammation among infected individuals. Findings shows that the prevalence appears unusually high among the study population. This emphasizes the need for routine antenatal screening and improved public awareness. Early detection can aid in reducing vertical transmission and ensuring better maternal and neonatal outcomes.
